title: The profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller monoid is a group, on a question of Lochak and Schneps
subject: math.GR
abstract: An element of the profinite Grothendieck-Teichmüller group $\widehat{\mathrm{GT}}$ of Drinfeld is a pair $(\lambda,f)$, with $\lambda$ a unit of $\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ and $f$ in the free profinite group $\widehat F_2$ on $x$ and $y$, that satisfies three relations and for which $x\mapsto x^\lambda$, $y\mapsto f^{-1}y^\lambda f$ is an automorphism of $\widehat F_2$. Lochak and Schneps asked in 2006 whether this last requirement follows from the others, and whether it holds with no relation at all (Question 1.1 of their list of open problems). We prove that it follows, and from less: if $\lambda\in1+2\widehat{\mathbb Z}$ and $f\in\widehat F_2$ satisfy the two-cycle and three-cycle relations (I) and (II), then $\lambda$ is a unit and the endomorphism is an automorphism. The pentagon relation is not used. Relation (I) alone does not suffice: for $\lambda=1$ and $f=xyx^{-1}y^{-1}$ the endomorphism is not surjective. It follows that the Grothendieck-Teichmüller monoid, in the profinite form of Horel and of Boavida de Brito, Horel and Robertson, is equal to its group of units; that every endomorphism of the profinite operad of parenthesized braids that fixes the objects is an automorphism; and, by their theorems, that every homotopy endomorphism of the profinite completion of the little 2-discs operad, or of the genus zero surface operad, is a homotopy automorphism. The proof counts boundary components of finite covers in homology. An endomorphism of the profinite completion of the fundamental group of a compact surface with boundary that sends every boundary generator to a conjugate of a unit power of a boundary generator, bijectively on boundary components, is an automorphism; on a sphere with at least three holes the exponents of such an endomorphism are equal, and are zero or a unit. The criterion for unit exponents and the case of unit $\lambda$ were produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode) and checked by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high. Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max checked them again, found the statements for exponents that are not assumed to be units and the example above, and wrote this text. Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max checked these additions independently. No human has checked any of it.
comments:
This note answers Question 1.1 of Lochak and Schneps, Open problems in Grothendieck-Teichmüller theory (Proc. Sympos. Pure Math. 74, 2006): is the invertibility requirement in the definition of the profinite group GT automatic? Yes, and already under the two-cycle and three-cycle relations: if lambda is in 1+2Z^ and f in F^_2 satisfy (I) and (II), then lambda is a unit and x -> x^lambda, y -> f^-1 y^lambda f is an automorphism (Theorem A). With no relation, or with (I) alone, it fails: lambda = 1, f = [x,y] (Proposition C). Consequences (Corollary D): the Grothendieck-Teichmüller monoid of Horel (arXiv:1504.01605, Definition 7.1) and of Boavida de Brito-Horel-Robertson (arXiv:1703.05143, Definition 7.2) equals its group of units; object-fixing endomorphisms of the profinite operad of parenthesized braids are automorphisms; by their Theorems 8.4 and 11.1, homotopy endomorphisms of the profinite completions of the little 2-discs operad and of the genus zero surface operad are automorphisms. Fresse's survey (arXiv:1811.12536, 2.6) records that no simple characterization of the invertible pairs was available in the profinite setting. Method: boundary classes of finite covers of a pair of pants in homology (Theorem E).

Checks: Theorem E(a) and the case of unit lambda were produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode) and checked step by step by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high (24 November 2026) and by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max (25 November 2026). The latter wrote the text and added Theorem E(b), by which lambda need not be assumed a unit and the pentagon is not needed, Proposition C, and the deduction of Corollary D; Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max checked these additions independently (25 November 2026). The operadic theorems are used as published. No human has checked the note; nothing in it is formalized. Records: https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/mathematics-workbenches

How it was produced. GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), in ChatGPT Pro mode, produced in a research run on Grothendieck's La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (returned 17 November 2026) the criterion for boundary-preserving endomorphisms with unit exponents (Theorem E(a) of the note), the third boundary relation (Lemma 3.1) and with them Theorem A for unit lambda; it noted that they answer the constrained form of Question 1.1 of Lochak and Schneps, gave an example in A_5 for f = [x,y]^2, and obtained the statement that the monoid is a group by a route through braid groups (Remark 5.3 of the note). Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), at effort max, wrote this text on 25 November 2026. It added Theorem E(b) (on a sphere with at least three holes the exponents are zero or a unit), which removes the hypothesis that lambda is a unit from Theorem A and makes the pentagon unnecessary for Corollary D(a); the observation that relation (I) holds for the examples; the examples in A_4 and S_3 of Proposition C; the deduction of Corollary D from the published operadic theorems; and the inductive derivation of the full-twist formula in Remark 5.3.

How it was checked. Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), at effort high, followed every step of the run's proofs of Theorem E(a) and Lemma 3.1 and of the torsion argument of Remark 5.3, and recomputed the A_5 example (24 November 2026); a second instance of Claude Opus 5.5, at effort high, searched the literature for the statements and opened Lochak-Schneps 2006 at Questions 1.1 and 1.2 (24 November 2026), and Claude Opus 5.5, at effort max, opened Dolgushev-Guynee at Definition 2.5. Claude Fable 5.2, at effort max, proved Theorem E(a) independently before reading the run's proof, recomputed Lemma 3.1 twice, and ran programs for the examples of Proposition C (both conventions for the product of permutations), for the boundary classes used in Theorem E(b) (covers with group (Z/p)^2, p = 2, 3, 5, 7), and for the braid identity of Remark 5.3 (n up to 6). It read Lochak-Schneps 2006 at the definition and at Question 1.1, Boavida de Brito-Horel-Robertson (arXiv:1703.05143v1) at Definitions 6.2, 6.10, 6.11, Lemma 7.1, Definition 7.2, Proposition 7.3 with its proof and Theorems 8.4 and 11.1, and Horel (arXiv:1504.01605v2) at Remark 4.20, Proposition 4.23, Corollary 4.24, Definition 7.1, Theorem 7.2, Proposition 7.4 and Theorem 8.4. Claude Opus 5.5, at effort max, in a separate run, checked Theorem E(b), the clause that lambda is a unit, Proposition C (by hand, in both conventions for the product of permutations) and the deduction of Corollary D, recomputed Lemma 3.1, and opened Lochak-Schneps 2006, Horel (Definition 7.1, Theorem 7.2, Proposition 7.4, Lemma 7.5, Theorem 8.4), Boavida de Brito-Horel-Robertson (Definition 7.2, Proposition 7.3, Theorems 8.4 and 11.1) and Fresse's survey (2.6, in its TeX) at the statements used (25 November 2026). Before posting, the main session, Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max, read the proofs of Theorems A and E, Lemma 3.1, Proposition C and Corollary D once more, step by step, and opened Harbater-Schneps 2000 at the definition of GT-hat_0 (section 0.1, p. 3118). The two derivations of the full-twist formula in Remark 5.3, which is not used in the proofs, have had no second reader. The proofs of the operadic theorems of Horel and of Boavida de Brito-Horel-Robertson were not checked by us. Drinfeld 1990 and Chow 1948 were not opened (the bibliographic data of Chow's paper were checked); the section numbers of Ribes-Zalesskii were confirmed in the publisher's table of contents, but not the statements inside them, and those of Serre's Cohomologie galoisienne in its third edition. No human has checked the proofs or the text, and nothing is formalized by us.
